technology.verdict: Yes — iPhone-only IMU (press-attitude yaw + integrated hand velocity) + ARKit placement is the RIGHT v1 sensing architecture for this specific product, because the product's promise is not measurement truth but honest, personalised, zero-equipment play — and every alternative that measures the swing better destroys the zero-equipment wedge that is the only validated reason this app exists (contrarian-verdict: only "hallway/hotel/lunch-break" use validates the premise; on a practice green a real ball wins). Rear-camera CV on a real ball (GoProPutt, Golfboy Putter Mode, Putt Vision are shipping existence proofs) is categorically better on outcome truth but is a tripod-and-equipment putting trainer — a different, crowded product that complements rather than replaces this build. ARKit body/hand tracking is topologically impossible here (the phone IS the club; the camera cannot watch the swinger). The Apple Watch lock should stay for v1: watchOS 10's CMBatchedSensorManager (800 Hz accel / 200 Hz device motion, Apple-marketed for golf impact detection) would cut timing quantization ~8x but is still an IMU in the same inference class, needs a HealthKit workout session, and halves the audience — it is a v2 accuracy option, not a different architecture. Of the two known IMU ceilings, the face-at-peak-velocity timing error (15–98 ms, up to −5.9°) is fixable within IMU-only — impact is a game-defined instant, not a physical event, and the harness already validated a re-approach that recovers ground truth on the same samples — while the 100%-face launch is fundamental (path is unmeasurable from a hand-held phone) but immaterial for putting (~95% face-determined) and correctly documented rather than faked. Bet: v1 = current stack + the H5 sampling fix + the missing honesty band; v1.5 = data-gated Watch spike + offline hand-path-proxy experiments through the existing replay harness; v2 = hybrid — optional real-ball camera mode that makes "a miss is a miss" literal AND serves as the free per-user ground-truth calibrator for air mode, a loop no competitor has.
strengths: The sensing choice matches the product physics: putting strokes are slow/smooth, so the phone's 100 Hz fused IMU is inside its validated envelope (gyro drift over a 1-2 s stroke ~0.5-2 deg, research-5 sec.1), unlike full swings where gyros saturate at ~1,627 deg/s (Nature 2024, research-1) — putting is the ONE golf motion an iPhone IMU can honestly sense

Press-attitude yaw delta is drift-robust by construction: face angle is a short-window relative rotation since press, immune to the magnetometer-indoors and ARKit-featureless-green failure modes the spec's original anchor design carried (realism-audit sec.3.3 documents this as a deliberate realism-for-robustness trade)

The architecture is uniquely tunable offline: the Linux harness compiles the app's real physics and replays 192 recorded strokes bit-identically (harness/README.md, PARITY GREEN 192/192), so estimator changes (like the H5 re-approach) converge without TestFlight cycles — a camera-CV architecture would forfeit this loop's simplicity

Honesty-about-uncertainty (snap-to-square, cause-not-result) is architecture-aligned: the system never displays a number the sensor can't defend, which is exactly the right posture for an inference-based sensor (GolfGo's structural failure is confident wrong calls on the same sensor class, research-1 sec.3)

Physics core is literature-grounded and portable: capture speed 1.626 m/s (Holmes/Hogan-Antali), cup radius, friction law verified against Penner/USGA (realism-audit sec.1) — this sim is reusable unchanged under ANY future sensing front-end, including a camera mode
Zero-equipment + press-during-stroke interaction is the shareability/free-to-try moat: no tripod, no ball, no Watch, works in a hallway — none of alternatives (a), (c), (d) can claim this
weaknesses: Face angle is inferred, not measured, and sampled at a moment with 15-98 ms of definitional slack (realism-audit sec.3.3, plab h5): up to -5.9 deg face error at 60 deg/s sweep — currently the single biggest sensing defect, and it is sitting fixable in the harness

The spec's own anti-GolfGo differentiator — the uncertainty band ('18 ft, est. 15-21 ft') — is NOT in the shipped AR result panel (realism-audit Gap #8); the architecture's honesty story is ahead of its UI

100%-face launch direction overstates directional punishment ~17% vs the real 83/17 face/path split (realism-audit Gap #5) — fundamental to hand-held IMU sensing; acceptable for putting but caps realism claims and must never be marketed as measurement

Press-declared-square semantics: a user who presses with a 4-deg open stance putts 'square' by definition (realism-audit sec.3.3) — the reference frame is self-relative, which is robust but means the app can never diagnose alignment faults, a thing real putting trainers do

No ground-truth anchor exists anywhere in the data: all 192 replays are air-swings with no external truth (harness/README.md 'Real-world roll distance has no truth anchor'); until a camera mode or tape-measure sessions exist, calibration converges on FEEL, not truth

The current v3 press-attitude face pipeline has never been validated against real recorded data (harness/README.md: no v2+ replays carry lock.attitudeAtPress; AR mode saves NO replays at all) — the architecture's most important signal path is the least evidenced

Peak-velocity integration remains spike-sensitive: the multi-km putt bug (realism-audit Gap #2) was clamped, not root-caused — single-integration of userAcceleration has no redundant cross-check in v1 (audio was lost with the ball; camera unused during stroke)

physics.verdict: The physics stack is the right foundation and is unusually well-grounded for an indie game: constant-decel roll with μ=0.611/S (Penner/Lee/Kolkowitz triangulated), Holmes/Hogan-Antali 1.626 m/s capture, vector-form friction, and semi-implicit Euler with overshoot-snap and segment cup detection — deterministic, bit-identical on the Linux harness, and with per-user calibration now bisecting the live simulator (S2 fix), the distance law is exact by construction. The audit's gap ranking is broadly correct; the two remaining arcade tells (dead-centre 180° bounce-back, over-generous off-centre capture) are one merged "hole model v1.1" fix, and the honesty display (Gap #8) is under-ranked given it IS the product thesis. But the realism ceiling does not live in the sim — it lives in the input: the IMU yields ~2 trustworthy scalars per stroke (peak hand speed ±5-10%, hand-yaw-since-press ±5-10°), so PuttingLab can max out as a superb distance-tempo-and-hole-feel putting game ("Wii putting with real green physics" — ~80% believable to non-golfers, ~60% to golfers per the synthesis's own estimate), never as a stroke analyzer: true face-vs-path, strike quality, and shot shape are structurally unreachable, and honest bucket/band/handicap design is the correct — and currently half-wired — compensator. The single biggest untapped realism lever is slope/break, precisely because it is the one golfer-visible realism dimension that comes entirely from the sim (which is fully controllable and already slope-ready in vector form) and not from the capped IMU input: the missing 40% of golfer-judged believability is slope+grain, the EoM and validation columns are already documented, and the physics is ~2 lines plus harness tests — the cost is the tilt-communication UX, not the math.
strengths: Literature-correct core constants, cited in code: cup radius 0.054 m (Rules of Golf), capture 1.626 m/s (Holmes 1991 / Hogan & Antali 2025 PMC12585879), μ_r(S)=0.611/S with the 5/7 rolling-inertia factor correctly absorbed once and reserved for slope gravity terms (BallPhysics.swift:39-52, 174-185; synthesis §2.4)

Calibration now closes the loop through the live simulator (v4 bisection over BallPhysics.simulatePutt, monotone by the maxLaunchSpeedMps saturation design, BallPhysics.swift:87-95) — the Gap #1 38%-short disaster class is structurally impossible to reintroduce
Vector-form friction (opposes instantaneous velocity, BallPhysics.swift:312-318) means curved slope trajectories emerge naturally — the sim is genuinely slope-ready, not slope-retrofittable

market.verdict: Air-swing golf on iPhone is real but tiny — a one-incumbent micro-niche, not a category. GolfGo (id 6753086848) is alive and shipping (v6.5, Jun 9 2026; 4.7 stars but only 892 US ratings, up ~190 in the 5 weeks since the repo's May-28 research captured 703 — order-of-magnitude tens of thousands of installs, versus Golf Clash's ~$3M/month and WGT's 22M lifetime downloads in the adjacent tap-golf category), and it is hard-paywalled at $49.99/yr behind a widely-hated subscription with no free tier. Critically, GolfGo's own v6.x release notes ("putt without the glitches") admit putting is its weakest, buggiest surface — PuttingLab attacks exactly the flank the incumbent is worst at, with the two fixes GolfGo's own reviewers demand (a real free tier and per-user calibration that stops the app lying about your misses). But be honest about the ceiling: the retention risk for a solo motion-gimmick game is severe (Phigolf sits at 3.3/2.6 stars despite years in market; GolfGo just bolted on Daily Streaks and weekly Club Standings because novelty decays), and 'honest uncertainty' is NOT feelable in session one — it is churn-prevention, felt only as the absence of GolfGo's "everything is a hook" frustration. Per-user calibration IS feelable (the "it read MY stroke" moment) and should carry the first session; honesty carries sessions 5-50. This is a free, shareable wedge product consistent with the contrarian verdict's PIVOT (ship free, capped spend) — not a revenue business in v1.
strengths: Incumbent's flank is exposed exactly where PuttingLab plays: GolfGo v6.5 release notes lead with putting-glitch fixes, its reviews complain of phantom hooks and a bait paywall, and its $49.99/yr no-free-tier model is the single most-named complaint in UK reviews ("£50 a year is too much... most people just won't do it") — PuttingLab shipping free with 5-stroke calibration is a direct counter to both.

Zero-hardware social invite is a structurally unserved 10/10 gap: every phone-only competitor either needs hardware (Phigolf: "the only catch? You have to convince your friends to buy it" — MyGolfSpy) or has no async challenge; PuttingLab can make the swing itself the social object at zero marginal friction.

Putting is the best possible air-swing sub-scope for the real JTBD (dead-time indoors): a putting stroke is socially and physically viable in an office/hallway/hotel room where a full driver swing is not, and putting is golf's most universally self-deprecating, banterable skill — ideal for group-chat challenges.

No competing no-ball putting product exists: every serious putting trainer (Puttr, Exputt $300-500, PuttOUT mats) requires a real ball and dedicated kit; camera apps (GolfBoy, GolfTrak, Swing Coach) require a tripod and a real ball. The phone-in-hand no-setup putting game slot is empty as of July 2026.

Engineering position is genuinely ahead of the incumbent on the trust axis: the 192-stroke replay harness, quantified face-timing error (15-98ms), and snap-to-square-when-uncertain contract mean PuttingLab can truthfully claim what GolfGo's reviewers say it fails at — and per-user calibration is demonstrable in the first 60 seconds.
weaknesses: Category size is unproven and small: the entire air-swing niche is one app with 892 US ratings; adjacent tap-golf scale (Golf Clash ~$3M/mo, WGT 22M downloads) proves golfers game on phones but with a couch mechanic — there is no evidence yet that motion golf retains at scale, and GolfGo's momentum (~38 new US ratings/week) is steady-small, not breakout.

Motion-gimmick retention risk is the dominant threat: Phigolf's 3.3 (UK Apple) / 2.6 (Google Play) ratings despite years of sales, the GolfWRX lament about attention spans of "more than six swings", and GolfGo's rapid addition of streaks + weekly standings all point to fast novelty decay for solo motion play; without the social loop, expect sub-10% D30.

The headline differentiator is partly invisible: 'honest uncertainty' cannot be felt in session one — users don't reward the absence of a bug they never met. Only calibration produces a feelable first-session moment; honesty-about-uncertainty is a retention property that marketing cannot lead with.

Putting-without-a-ball has a substitution problem the full swing doesn't: a real ball plus any carpet and a mug is free and higher-fidelity, so the product only wins in contexts where even that is impractical (office, travel, queue) — the contrarian verdict's test stands: if early users say they'd use it 'on the practice green', the premise is dead.

GolfGo's developer (GETCALLERID LLC) is actively iterating monthly and already owns the 'swing your phone' mindshare and ASO position; if PuttingLab's free calibration wedge visibly works, the incumbent can copy calibration faster than PuttingLab can build courses, multiplayer, and content depth.

Solo-founder opportunity cost (per docs/contrarian-verdict.md): plausible Y1 UK paying ceiling ~£14.5k with LTV/CAC ~0.04 against golf-vertical UAC — this cannot be a paid-acquisition business; it lives or dies on organic shareability.

gtm.verdict: Ship it — but stop building. The remaining Definition-of-Done is no longer an engineering problem: 5 of the spec §14's 8 items are code-complete (335 tests green, S2 calibration fix, edge-case hardening), and the 3 open items — golfer says "feels right" 4/5 (§14.3), iPhone 12–17 device matrix (§14.7), ≥2 external TestFlight testers (§14.8) — are all humans-and-distribution work. The build has already overshot the spec badly (spec said 2D top-down, no AR, 14 days; the repo is at v0.7.15 of an 80-brief backlog with AR cup placement, replay history, and screen recording), and the one thing the GTM actually depends on is missing: there is zero player-facing share mechanic — the only UIActivityViewController usages ship developer JSON/logs (ReplayHistoryView.swift, ARLogShareSheet.swift), and both result panels are text rows with no share button, no celebration capture, no replay-to-video. Monetisation should be one-time unlock (~$4.99/£3.99) added in v1.1, never subscription: GolfGo's own 892-rating page shows the subscription-required model generating exactly the review backlash ("misleading… subscription is mandatory") that PuttingLab's free-to-try honesty positioning is built to exploit, and a UserDefaults-only app with no server costs cannot justify recurring billing. Distribution is TikTok/Reels-led (a person swinging a phone at an invisible ball into an AR cup is a native curiosity hook, and zero-follower accounts can break out under TikTok's interest-pool algorithm) but not TikTok-only — r/golf, James's golf club, and ASO against a beatable 892-rating incumbent complete it. The async friend challenge was rightly deferred as backend infrastructure but wrongly deferred in spirit: a screenshot-share challenge card costs no backend and belongs in v1; the real version should ship in v1.1 via Game Center (still no backend). Honour the contrarian verdict's caps: £79 + bounded weekly hours, and a hard kill/proceed gate at week 3 using its three device tests before any further investment.
strengths: DoD is nearly closed on the engineering side: spec §14 items 1,2,4,5,6 are code-complete — 335 tests green, offline harness replays 192 recorded strokes bit-identically, S2 calibration fix landed (docs/realism-audit-2026-07-02.md §1 row 16: calibration now bisects the live physics, 'exact by construction'), and pre-TestFlight hardening (scenePhase, AR interruption, permission-denied flows) is committed (docs/testflight-handoff.md).

The honesty positioning has a live, documented enemy weakness: GolfGo (id 6753086848) is free-to-download but subscription-REQUIRED ($8.99/mo, $49.99/yr) and its reviews complain about the hidden mandatory paywall and 'registers hooks inconsistently' — PuttingLab's free-to-try + snap-to-square-when-uncertain contract attacks both complaints directly.

The share infrastructure already exists in the codebase, just pointed at developers: ARScreenRecorder.swift wraps ReplayKit end-to-end and ShareSheet/UIActivityViewController wrappers exist (ReplayHistoryView.swift:316-322) — turning these into a player-facing putt-replay share is days, not weeks.

The product demos natively on short video: a human swinging a phone like a putter with no ball, then an AR ball rolling to a real-looking cup, is a self-explanatory 3-second hook — the rare category where the gameplay IS the ad.

Zero-backend architecture (UserDefaults, no networking — spec §7) means launch carries no infra cost, no privacy-nutrition-label complexity (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy already declares no tracking), and the kill-switch costs nothing: a dead app stays live free.

The phone→Drive→laptop replay tuning loop is a real beta accelerator: 20 testers' strokes can be replayed under parameter variants offline and shipped in one build — most solo founders have nothing like this for a motion game.
weaknesses: The spec bets on social sharing but the current build produces no shareable moment: PracticeSessionView's ResultPhaseView renders debug rows ('face (raw)', 'peak velocity', 'confidence' — PracticeSessionView.swift:423-478) and the AR StrokeResultPanel.swift has only headline/bucket/cause + 'Putt again'/'Reset all' — no share button, no make-celebration, no auto-captured replay video. As shipped, the GTM's core mechanic does not exist.

No monetisation section exists anywhere in the contract: spec §14 defines done, GOAL.md lists 'Pricing' only under 'Stop and ask James', and the contrarian verdict recommended deferring the paywall — so v1 has no instrumentation to learn what users would pay for (not even a local counter of free-play-gate hits).

Scope creep already consumed the calendar: the spec was a 14-day, 2D, no-AR build (locked decision #6); the repo is 80 briefs deep with AR placement, hole options, stance renders, replay history — each additional brief now trades directly against the 3 human DoD items that actually block launch.

≥48% of §14 open items depend on other people and none are scheduled: no named external testers (§14.8), no golfer feel sign-off (§14.3), no iPhone 12 low-end device test (§14.7); docs/feedback/ is empty and the TestFlight upload still needs a mate's signing team or a £79 account (docs/testflight-handoff.md §1).

Realism gaps sit exactly where share-clips would expose them: capture is over-generous off-centre and dead-centre lip-outs kick straight back (docs/realism-audit-2026-07-02.md gaps #3/#7) — a viral clip of an obviously-wrong lip-out is negative marketing; also spec-drift on display angles (uncapped, audit row 13) can show silly numbers on camera.

The contrarian verdict's economics still stand un-rebutted: £14.5k plausible UK Y1 ceiling and LTV/CAC ≈ 0.04 means paid UA is permanently off the table — the whole plan lives or dies on organic short-video + community, and TikTok organic realistically needs 2-3 posts/day for 60-90 days to produce consistent installs, which collides with a 3DPE day job unless content creation is batched during beta sessions.

App identity is not launch-ready: placeholder green 'PL' icon, bundle ID com.puttinglab.app possibly taken, no screenshots/preview video, no ASO keyword work — and a motion game cannot be conveyed by stills, so the App Store preview video is mandatory work nobody has scheduled.

contrarian.verdict: PROCEED — but narrowly, re-scoped as a 30-day validation experiment, not a product build, and only because the KILL case is unmeasured rather than refuted. Re-litigating the earlier council (docs/contrarian-verdict.md, verdict: PIVOT, cap "£79 Apple fee + 3 days"): its technical kill has been genuinely repaired since (192/192 bit-identical off-device parity, the S2 calibration bug that made every calibrated putt roll ~38% of promise found and fixed, 335 tests green), but its spending cap was blown by ~29 calendar days and its single most important test — the cold-eye 3-golfer test it called "the only test that touches the unfalsifiable layer" — is still the only test never run. Thirty-four days and ~205 commits after the spec was written, docs/feedback/ is empty, all 192 recorded strokes are James's own, TestFlight distribution still depends on borrowing "your mate's" Apple Developer Team ID, and the spec's only two done-criteria requiring another human (§14.3 golfer says "feels right" 4/5; §14.8 ≥2 testers beyond James) are precisely the two unmet. Worse, the product's stated differentiator — honesty-about-uncertainty — is not in the build: the "18 ft (est. 15–21 ft)" band doesn't exist in the AR path (realism audit Gap #8), the MarioKart assist layer is decorative, and tempo was never built; today's build is closer to "GolfGo with better tests," competing on the exact accuracy dimension the JTBD research says is where everyone else dies. PIVOT loses on inspection: every adjacent target (tempo trainer: market adequately served, gap 3/10; camera putting trainer: different tech stack against a free incumbent; B2B physics licensing: no distribution, no identified buyer; accessibility: genuine but micro) is weaker than the current wedge, so the real pivot option is intra-product — reposition around the gap-10 async-challenge JTBD (C2) if solo practice fails to retain. The development approach is the core finding: AI agents made engineering nearly free, so the system bought more of it — parity harnesses, five audit documents, a council of skeptics — while the binding constraint (does any golfer open it twice?) costs £79 and a group-chat message. The one decision this month: pay the £79, ship the current build to 10 external golfers by 9 July with kill thresholds pre-registered in the repo BEFORE the first install, and freeze all engineering except the missing honesty band. If fewer than ~3/10 testers return unprompted within a week, execute the earlier council's verdict for real.
strengths: PROCEED case, technical: the earlier council's technical kill (Voice 2) is empirically repaired — harness/README.md shows PARITY GREEN 192/192 with max |delta| = 0.0 (bit-identical glibc vs Darwin), 327 portable tests + 335 total green, and the zero-copy design makes app/harness drift structurally impossible; break-fix history shows 24 critical bugs fixed across 5 cycles.

PROCEED case, economics: the offline tuning loop (phone strokes -> Drive -> laptop replay in seconds) removed the device-in-the-loop bottleneck for physics/feel iteration — the S2 bug (calibrated putts rolling 0.385x the promised distance, confirmed by b79 device data) was caught and fixed offline before any external user ever saw it; that bug would have been a first-session killer.

PROCEED case, market: the wedge is real and documented — research-2 rates 'pocket boredom-killer' C1 gap 9/10 and 'async friend challenge, no hardware' C2 gap 10/10 with zero phone-only apps serving either; GolfGo's two most-quoted failures (paywall-before-magic at £49.99/yr, dishonest physics 'everything hooks') map one-to-one onto PuttingLab's locked decisions (free-to-try, per-user calibration, snap-to-square honesty).

PROCEED case, category validation: GolfGo is alive on the App Store (id 6753086848, https://apps.apple.com/us/app/golfgo-swing-your-phone/id6753086848) at 4.7/5 with 703 US ratings per research-2's counter-evidence section — demand for the concept exists; the incumbent's execution and pricing are the openings.

Rare intellectual honesty in the artifacts themselves: the realism audit documents its own product's divergences from literature (Penner, Holmes 1991, Hogan & Antali 2025) with file:line citations, and the repo contains a hostile council verdict it chose to keep — the raw material for a genuinely honest product exists.

The harness itself is standalone IP: compiling an iOS app's production Swift sources unmodified on Linux/Docker with a simd shim and replay-golden parity gating is a transferable dev-tooling asset for any sensor-driven app, independent of PuttingLab's fate.
weaknesses: KILL steelman #1 — zero user evidence after 34 days: docs/feedback/ has been empty since its creation on May 29; all 192 replays are schemaVersion-1 strokes from James's own builds 7–16; spec §14 items 3 and 8 (the only two done-criteria requiring a human other than James) are the only ones unmet; the 12 Prolific interviews the earlier council priced at £100 were never run. The category benchmark makes this lethal: 'good' day-3 retention for arcade/casual titles is only ~23–30% (https://appagent.com/blog/mobile-game-retention-benchmarks/), and a solo-loop novelty app with no social object plausibly retains far below that — and v1 ships none of C2, the one gap-10 retention engine the project's own research identified.

verdict.verdict: YES on the design, NO on the order of operations. The architecture and physics are right — verified right, not just argued right — but the product's stated differentiator is the one thing not built, and 34 days of engineering happened before the one £79 test that decides whether the app should exist. Three strongest reasons: (1) The sensing architecture is correct and should never be re-litigated: iPhone-only IMU (press-attitude yaw + peak hand velocity) + ARKit placement is the ONLY architecture that preserves the validated zero-equipment hallway/hotel wedge — putting is the one golf motion inside the iPhone IMU's honest envelope (full-swing gyros saturate at ~1,627°/s; putting never approaches it), ARKit body tracking is topologically impossible (the phone IS the club), Watch halves the audience for the same inference class, and camera-CV-on-a-real-ball is a different, crowded product (GoProPutt, Golfboy) that requires the tripod the JTBD forbids. The physics core is literature-grounded (Penner/Holmes/Hogan-Antali, cited at file:line), calibration is now exact-by-construction (v4 bisection, S2 fixed), and 192/192 bit-identical Linux replay parity gives a tuning loop most teams never get. (2) But the differentiated product does not exist in the build — I verified it: StrokeResultPanel.swift:163 formats raw face angle to one decimal ("+7.3°"), directly violating the project's own honesty rule; the "18 ft (est. 15–21 ft)" uncertainty band has zero grep hits in the AR result path; the MarioKart bucket layer is decorative (sim and display consume faceAngleRaw); tempo was never built; and the only UIActivityViewController usages ship developer JSON/logs — there is no player-facing share moment at all. What is TestFlight-ready today is "GolfGo with better tests", competing on the exact accuracy axis where the JTBD research says everyone dies. (3) The process is inverted and the prior verdict was ignored: docs/feedback/ is empty (created May 29, zero files), all 192 recorded strokes are James's own, the contrarian council's "£79 Apple fee + 3 days" cap was exceeded by ~29 calendar days, and its one binding test — 3 cold-eye golfers — was never run. AI-agent velocity made engineering nearly free, so the project bought more engineering instead of evidence. The binding constraint is "does any golfer open it twice, and where?" — it costs £79 and a group-chat message, and it is answerable within 7 days. So: keep the design, freeze the build, ship the honesty layer that IS the product, and put the current app in 10 strangers' hands by 9 July with kill thresholds committed to the repo before the first invite.
